candidates.source_title: Strikes back on at four Greater Manchester hospitals after payment offer withdrawals, says UNISON
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
More than 350 Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust (NCA) employees, including nurses, clinical support workers, and housekeepers at Rochdale Infirmary, Royal Oldham Hospital, Fairfield Hospital in Bury, and Salford Royal Hospital are walking out on Monday 24th, Wednesday 26th, and Friday 28th August.

UNISON says an offer to resolve the dispute was initially tabled by NCA bosses but withdrawn before discussions could take place.

The row centres on the trust's use of an outside agency (NHS Professionals (NHSP)) to manage overtime.

When covering staff shortages, staff are entitled to time-and-a-half pay. However, the union says that in some cases, staff would earn less than they would on a normal shift, with some missing out on more than £80 per shift.

Operating theatre staff were previously on picket lines at all four aforementioned sites in June.

UNISON North West regional organiser Kevin Dolan said: “Those at the top of NCA have shown a lack of leadership and made their disregard for their staff clear.

“A deal was put on the table but taken away before we had chance to talk it over. We are ready to continue negotiations, but it’s obvious NCA has no intention of resolving this.

“This isn’t complicated. Staff are simply asking for what their contract says they’re entitled to. Nothing more.”

Staff from all four sites will gather in Salford on Wednesday 26th August for a unified day of protest.
candidates.source_summary: Hundreds of NHS operating theatre staff at four hospitals in Greater Manchester will be back on strike for three days next week in a dispute about overtime payments, says UNISON

The new play area will include accessible play towers, swings with cradle seats, a horse springer, slide, climbing net, and a wheelchair-accessible roundabout, along with sensory and social play panels designed to support imaginative play for younger children.

It will also include colourful wet pour safety surfacing and a new tarmac path linking the existing ramp to the new equipment, making the space easier to access and enjoy.

New bench seating will provide parents and carers with a place to sit while children play.

Councillor Tricia Ayrton, Deputy Leader of the Council, and Portfolio Holder for Climate Change and Environment, said: "This new play area at Lower Place has been designed to give local children of all abilities more opportunities to play, whether on their own or with friends. candidates.source_title: Courteeners’ Liam Fray to voice tram announcements for concerts - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Courteeners’ frontman Liam Fray will be helping tram users find their way to Wythenshawe Park this week, with the star providing on-stop announcements for a run of major concerts at the venue this weekend. The Middleton indie-rockers are one of the big names playing at Wythenshawe Park between Friday, August 21, and Sunday, August 30, with other headliners including The Cure, Lewis Capaldi, Pulp, and The Prodigy. Fans travelling by tram will hear the frontman’s voice on each date – including special announcements for the Middleton indie-rockers show on August 29. There will be as many double trams as possible running from the city centre every seven-and-a-half minutes. Concertgoers are advised to travel on the Airport line to Moor Road tram stop, which is around a 10-minute walk from the concert entrance. There will also be dedicated shuttle buses for all five concerts, providing direct connections from Manchester city centre and East Didsbury to Wythenshawe Park. Buses from the city centre will depart from Aytoun Street, close to Manchester Piccadilly, every six minutes, while services from East Didsbury’s Parrs Wood will run every 15 minutes. Shuttle buses will also operate after each concert to help fans return to East Didsbury and the city centre. Fans can buy an event travel pass for £8 per event day, which can be used on any combination of Bee Network bus, tram or shuttle bus on the event days. This can be bought in advance on the Bee Network app. A number of regular Bee Network bus services also stop close to Wythenshawe Park, including the 41, 103, 370 and 371 on Palatine Road and 11, 248 and 249 on Altrincham Road. People intending to travel on these services should check the Bee Network app or website before travelling as some diversions will be in place on event days.

candidates.source_title: Greater Manchester to receive £17m in funding to help with the homelessness crisis
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The Greater Manchester Combined Authority is to receive £16,955,174 over three years in an attempt to tackle rough sleeping in the area as part of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's national drive to end rough sleeping that totals £442 million across the country over three years, and £37 million in the North West.

The money is to create new accommodation and support that is to be rolled out across England this winter.

Alongside emergency accommodation for those who are rough sleepers, the programme will offer help with housing, health, and other needs, in an attempt to help people build a more stable future, rather than just giving people a temporary place to stay.

Accompanying this initiative, Burnham has announced that he will host a national summit in the Autumn to bring together leaders from business, finance, charities, health, faith communities, and more to ask what role each of them could play in ending rough sleeping.

Crisis, a charity for people who are homeless, suggest that preventing 40,000 people from becoming homeless could save the taxpayer close to £370 million.

PM Andy Burnham has said:  “No-one should have to bed down in a doorway or outside a station. But we’ve seen it for so long that it feels like Westminster has started to accept it.

"I won’t accept it. That’s why my first instruction as Prime Minister was to end rough sleeping. And it’s why today we’re getting started with a national drive to get everyone in for Christmas.

"We did it in the pandemic. We can do it again. But it needs all of us. Government will put the money in. But I’m asking leaders in communities and sectors across society to play their part locally too.

"Let’s get people out the cold. And let’s bring back hope."

Of the money in the initiative, £8.4 million of the new funding is going specifically to the Ending Homelessness in Communities Fund. This takes total funding allocations announced for 100 different projects to £47 million over three years.

As well as off the street provision, the funding will help local areas deliver more than 1000 settled homes over the next three years, alongside further wraparound support to help people rebuild their lives. Labour say that areas facing the greatest pressures will receive the largest share of support, with communities all across England getting support to address rough sleeping in their area.

Alongside funding allocations, the Government is publishing guidance to help local areas mobilise quickly and deliver a consistent route off the street offer this winter. The guidance will make clear the need to ensure adequate and accessible provision for women experiencing rough sleeping, recognising that women are often underrepresented in official statistics and may be at greater risk of violence, abuse, and exploitation. Guidance encourages local areas to consider single sex accommodation with specialist, intensive and trauma informed support, for victims of domestic abuse and sexual violence. This will support the government’s commitment to halve violence against women and girls in the next ten years.

This funding comes after Andy Burnham gave his first instruction to end rough sleeping across the country.
candidates.source_summary: Through a £442 million package, the North West is to receive £37m to curb rough sleeping to get people in for the winter

candidates.source_title: Rochdale says goodbye to ‘a force for joy’ — the one and only Jimmy Cricket - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale will have a chance to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral next week. Jimmy died on August 3, aged 80, after a short illness with his family around him. Known for his clean humour, the Northern Ireland comedian became a household name in the 1970s after working the comedy club scene. Famous for his catchphrase “And there’s more”, he lived in Rochdale and was a big supporter of local charities and causes. On Thursday, August 20, his body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church in Rochdale from 3pm to 5pm on for anyone wanting to pay their respects. His life will then be celebrated at Salford Cathedral starting with a vigil mass for the reception of the body at 7pm. It will be followed by his funeral at 1.30pm on Friday, August 21, at the cathedral, with mourners encouraged to wear bow ties which, along with his Wellington boots, became Jimmy’s trademark. Known for his clean humour, the Northern Ireland comedian became a household name in the 1970s after working the comedy club scene. candidates.source_title: Exciting new netball partnership launched to inspire players and boost sport across Rochdale - InYourArea
candidates.source_body_excerpt: One of the borough's leading sports clubs joins forces with the town's professional football team to widen access to physical activity Rochdale AFC, Rochdale AFC Community Trust and Rochdale Netball Club are delighted to announce the launch of Rochdale AFC Netball. The agreement will see Rochdale Netball Club rebrand and become part of the club's wider 'Our Teams' family. The partnership brings together one of the borough's leading community sports clubs with its professional football club and official charitable arm, creating a stronger platform to grow netball and widen access to physical activity across Rochdale — from primary school participation through to junior and adult club netball, coaching, volunteering and leadership. Netball is one of the most widely played team sports in England, particularly among women and girls, with accessible formats for all ages and abilities, including junior netball, Back to Netball and Walking Netball. Under the new Rochdale AFC Netball identity, the partnership will raise the sport's profile locally, strengthen school-to-club links, and give more people a clear route into the game. Currently, Rochdale Netball Club runs teams from under-sixes right through to seniors, with nearly 200 players taking to the court every week. The agreement will also support wider community outcomes, with Rochdale AFC Community Trust working alongside Rochdale AFC Netball on new programmes in schools, holiday provision, health and wellbeing, and volunteer development. Operating under a shared Rochdale AFC identity opens up new opportunities too, from commercial support and matchday promotion to community events and sponsorship, reinforcing that women's sport has a central place in the borough's sporting future. The move follows a model seen elsewhere in professional sport, where football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to boost visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. In Rochdale, the priority will be a community-first approach that reflects the town's sporting pride and welcomes people of all ages.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale's biggest housing estate is about to get even bigger - Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale’s largest housing estate is about to get even bigger now plans for more homes have been approved. The Kirkholt estate will get a new 23-home apartment block and five terraced houses off Queen’s Drive. The developer, Mosscare St Vincent Housing (MSV), says all the homes would be available for social rent (around 60 per cent of market rates). The idea behind this scheme is to bring ‘much-needed’ affordable housing to the area. Click here for the latest on Greater Manchester's politics in our newsletter MSV is a not-for-profit Registered Provider who own and manage almost 9,000 homes across Greater Manchester, Lancashire and West Yorkshire. The apartments would all be one-beds and the terraced homes would contain four-bedrooms each. The site where the homes will be built currently sits empty. An old block of flats used to sit on the land next to the A664 (Queensway), but it was demolished in 2009. It was used as a temporary space by Kirkholt Medical Practice for a short time before the health centre got its permanent digs down the road. Planning papers read: “The application site is a prominent site within the local area. The intention is to create a high-quality sustainable development that addresses housing needs and meets the needs of the local community. “This proposal has been developed in response to an identified local demand, helping to reduce anti-social behaviour issues and the various problems associated with the site in its disused state. “By redeveloping the former brownfield site, we plan on increasing the benefits of its regeneration by utilising vacant land and delivering affordable homes for local residents. “MSV’s vision for this site is to create a secure outward looking scheme for social rent. They want to provide housing, with the aim of creating a balanced community and to promote tenure diversification in the area.” Plans for a new community garden, to compliment the scheme, were also approved last month. It would be run by Q Gardens, a community group that already operates in the Kirkholt area.

However, they said that the UK’s insistence on deporting Ahmed to Pakistan after his release from prison could damage existing agreements on migrant returns and affect broader cooperation on intelligence, security and organised crime. Pakistani officials also expressed concern over reports suggesting that Britain could impose measures such as visa restrictions on Pakistani nationals and reductions in foreign aid if Islamabad continued to reject Ahmed’s return. British authorities are seeking to increase the deportation of foreign offenders to ease pressure on overcrowded prisons. Official figures show that 306 Pakistani nationals are being held in UK prisons as of June 30. Ahmed was released from prison last month after serving 14 years of a 22-year sentence for multiple child rape convictions. British Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced plans to amend immigration laws to remove a legal barrier that prevented the Home Office from deporting Ahmed after his British citizenship was revoked. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Council has set out the support it offers young people in care as they become adults. Young people, councillors, members of Rochdale’s Parents Carers Voice and council staff came together for the launch of the council’s new Preparing for Adulthood strategy at a special event held at Spotland Mills, Rochdale. Preparing for adulthood is about making the journey easier, clearer and more positive for young people aged 14 to 25, as well as the families and carers who support them. The council’s Preparing for Adulthood Team helps young people find the best support when moving from children’s services into adult social care. Before young people turn 18, the council completes an assessment to identify care and support needs. For those eligible, it will create new support plan to help young adults continue with their education, help them develop new skills and find any additional support the young person or their family might need. candidates.source_body_excerpt: US actress Hayden Panettiere, best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, has died aged 36. A representative for the actress confirmed the death to US network ABC News on Sunday, saying her family would remember her “incredible light” who brought “immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her”. The statement from her father Skip read: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. No cause of death has been announced. The 36-year-old began acting as a child, appearing in soap operas before gaining wider recognition for her role in the 2000 sports drama Remember The Titans alongside Denzel Washington, and as the voice of Dot in 1998’s A Bug’s Life. Panettiere later found fame playing cheerleader Claire Bennet in the superhero drama Heroes before going on to star as up-and-coming country singer Juliette Barnes for six seasons on the hit TV series Nashville. Her film credits include 2006’s Bring It On: All Or Nothing, comedy-drama film Raising Helen, and appearances in Scream 4 and Scream VI as Kirby Reed. Following her rapid rise to fame, the pressure of the industry began to weigh on Panettiere – with the actress previously revealing that she had struggled with addiction throughout her 20s. In a memoir published earlier this year, Panettiere opened up about her struggles with mental health, the loss of her younger brother, Jansen, and her decision to give full custody of her daughter to her former partner, Ukrainian boxer Wladimir Klitschko.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A retired police officer has returned to his old station more than 60 years after starting his career. Allan Murray, now 93, visited Rochdale police station to share memories from his time as an officer, which began in 1959 when he joined the force at the age of 22. During his visit, Mr Murray brought a collection of photographs and stories from his years in service, including images from his training at Bruche Police Training Centre. A photo of PC Allan Murray's during his career (Image: Greater Manchester Police) His great-granddaughter, PC Sophie Brown, currently serves with Greater Manchester Police and is also based in Rochdale. PC Brown said: "I’ve always had so much respect and love for my great grandad. "I’ve been so grateful to follow in his footsteps and honour him in the career that I’m doing. "It was amazing to be able to show him around the station and bring him back to his ‘good old days’.

candidates.source_title: Jamie Dallimore double drives Rochdale Hornets comeback at Workington Town - Total Rugby League
candidates.source_body_excerpt: WORKINGTON TOWN 20 ROCHDALE HORNETS 22 DAVE PARKINSON, Fibrus Community Stadium, Sunday ROCHDALE held off their hosts to clinch a first league win in seven attempts. Hornets made a strong start, and led 6-0, but were then 14-6 behind before mounting their own comeback. When Town were penalised early on, Max Flanagan slotted the goal, and his side extended their advantage after ten minutes when Harvey Braddish was hauled down by the line and Ross Whitmore dived in from dummy-half. Flanagan was unable to convert. The visitors were having much the better of the contest for the first 25 minutes with Mark Ioane, Jordan Syme and Chris Barratt enjoying their forays at the Workington pack. With some handling errors added to the mix, the hosts found themselves in a midfield slog. But they gradually began to turn the screw and were unfortunate with two chances. The first came after half an hour when Evan Lawther brushed away from two defenders on the left and went to Oscar Doran, who sped into the backfield, but with the support of debutant Jaiden Tallantire and Jake Carter inside, the pass went between both players. Then a wonderful pass from Tallantire undid Rochdale on the right – but Zarrin Galea couldn’t take the ball cleanly.

Operating under a shared Rochdale AFC identity will also open new opportunities from commercial support and matchday promotion to community events and sponsorship. It will boost visibility, participation and long-term sustainability, with the priority of a community-first approach that reflects the town’s sporting pride and welcomes people of all ages. Amy Williams, Chair of Rochdale AFC Netball, said: “This is a fantastic opportunity for our club and for netball across Rochdale. Joining the Rochdale AFC family gives us a stronger platform to grow the game, inspire more women and girls to get involved, and create new opportunities for players, coaches, volunteers and supporters. candidates.source_title: The Rochdale pioneer still being honoured at the White House - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The legacy of a Rochdale reformer is still being recognised in the White House after more than 160 years. John Bright was born in Greenbank in 1811. He was a Quaker, politician, statesman, social reformer and British radical. He became friends with the US President Abraham Lincoln and the pair enjoyed a special relationship of mutual respect. A chance conversation and some digging by a Rochdale Town Hall volunteer have revealed that a bust made in tribute to him is still on display at the White House today. Lincoln had a portrait of Bright on the walls of his reception room. The bust was commissioned by Manchester solicitor Thomas Blain as a gift for the president who was assassinated before it was presented to him. The bust was added to the White House collection under President Johnson. Mayoress of Rochdale Iram Faisal shared on Facebook: “Wow! What a discovery! Never in my life could I have imagined that a chance conversation with one of our town hall volunteers would lead to such an incredible piece of history. “While talking about the fascinating history of Rochdale Town Hall, the subject of John Bright came up — our very own Rochdale-born politician, cotton manufacturer, philanthropist and one of the most influential figures of the 19th century. “John Bright was a strong supporter of Abraham Lincoln and the Union during the American Civil War, and his connection with Lincoln is a remarkable part of our shared history.

First-half goals from summer signings Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe put the Exiles in charge at a sun-baked Rodney Parade.

Any hopes of a Rochdale fightback were ended by Bilongo's dismissal and Bamba lashed in a third in stoppage time to add to their misery.

candidates.source_title: Hayden Mullins believes Newport County can build on victory over Rochdale - South Wales Argus
candidates.source_body_excerpt: HAYDEN Mullins is convinced there is a lot more to come from his Newport County AFC team, despite a superb opening-day win over Rochdale. County cruised to a 3-0 victory over the newly-promoted visitors, who were already 2-0 down when they were reduced to 10 men midway through the second half. First-half goals from Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe and a late third from Yahya Bamba secured a first three points of the League Two season and made it a near-perfect day for the Exiles at a sun-drenched Rodney Parade. Dale didn't have a shot on target all afternoon, but Mullins believes there is still room for improvement from his side. "We know that we need to make our home form really positive this season and we wanted to lay a marker down and I think we did that," said the manager. "The boys deserve massive credit because they went about their jobs really well. They've really responded to what I'm trying to put across, they believe in the work that we've been doing and they put in a real good shift. "But I think there's definitely another level. I don't think this is us. It's the first game of the [league] season and there's definitely more levels. "Our fitness can definitely come up and there were more opportunities to score as well. "I'm so pleased for the boys that got the goals - [especially] Shaq and Yahya," he added. "That will give them such a lift.

candidates.source_title: Hayden Mullins happy as Newport ‘lay marker down’ against Rochdale - London Now
candidates.source_body_excerpt: New Newport manager Hayden Mullins believes his side have made a statement of intent with a comprehensive 3-0 home win over newly-promoted Rochdale in their League Two opener. First-half goals from summer signings Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe put the Exiles in charge and Dale’s return to the fourth tier went from bad to worse when left-back Bryant Bilongo was shown a second yellow card midway through the second half before Yahya Bamba made it 3-0 in stoppage time. County fans had to wait until December 29 for their first home win of last season but Mullins was delighted to earn three points at Rodney Parade at the first attempt, even if it could have been more comfortable had Christian Doidge and Ciaran Brennan not been superbly denied by visiting goalkeeper Nils Ramming. “We know that we need to make our home form really positive this season and we wanted to lay a marker down and I think we did that,” said Mullins. “The boys deserve massive credit because they went about their jobs really well. They’ve really responded to what I’m trying to put across, they believe in the work that we’ve been doing and they put in a real good shift. “The noise was fantastic,” added the former West Ham United and Crystal Palace midfielder. “But I think we know we’ve got to give the fans something to shout about. We’ve got to be more aggressive in what we do out of possession and we applied pressure in the right areas. I’m really pleased with the performance.” It was a different story for Rochdale boss Ian Watson, who replaced promotion-winning manger Jimmy McNulty after he departed for Stockport County during the summer. “It was not good,” admitted Watson. “It’s a tough moment for us, for sure. Newport are good at what they do and we knew that if we allowed them to feed balls into the box continuously it was going to be hard for us. And we didn’t prevent them from getting balls into the box, we didn’t prevent set-pieces and we weren’t brave enough with the ball.”
